frame.origin: Centre of the base at the original pavement. Interior inches are Petrie's centre. The exterior square uses Cole's mean side, which differs from Petrie's base by 16 mm.
frame.x: east, metres, before the true-north rotation
frame.z: north, metres, before the true-north rotation
frame.rotation: The whole monument is rotated about +Y so the north face points west of true north by the chosen azimuth. Feature coordinates in this file are in the pyramid frame, before that rotation.
frame.inchNote: Petrie's inch is the British inch of 1880–83, converted here at exactly 25.4 mm.

mast.reported: 29°58′45.05570″ N, 31°08′03.11209″ E, centre of the base of the summit mast

baseCenterFromMastMetres.reported: Mast at N 100,000.260, E 499,999.623 against a base-centre origin of N 100,000, E 500,000. The base centre is therefore 0.260 m south and 0.377 m east of the mast.

obsoleteHelmert.note: Published Helmert-ellipsoid position. Plots about 180 m west of the pyramid on WGS84. Not used.

disagreements.chosen: 230.36375 m, the mean of Cole's four sides
disagreements.range: 230.253 m (Cole north) to 230.454 m (Cole south); Petrie mean 230.348 m; Dash 2015 mean about 230.353 m (755 ft 9 in)
disagreements.why: Cole 1925 measured the casing foot with invar wires. Petrie's 1883 mean and Dash's 2015 mean sit 11–16 mm away, inside the corner-socket uncertainty Petrie himself discussed.

disagreements.chosen: 51°52′00″ (Petrie's measured casing angle) applied to Cole's mean base, giving 146.721 m
disagreements.range: Petrie 51°52′ ± 2′. The seked of 5½ palms is atan(14/11) = 51°50′34″, inside that tolerance. Petrie's own height, from his base and this angle, is 5,776 ± 7 inches (146.710 m).
disagreements.why: The mesh has to be one triangle. Using the measured angle on the chosen base keeps the slope and the height consistent. The 11 mm gap with Petrie's height is smaller than his ±7 inch tolerance.

disagreements.chosen: 3′06.25″ west of true north, the mean of Cole's four side deviations
disagreements.range: Cole's sides differ among themselves from 1′57″ to 5′30″. Petrie's casing mean is −3′43″.
disagreements.why: Cole's azimuths are tied to the same casing-foot lines as the chosen base. The sides are not parallel, so a single rotation is a mean.

disagreements.range: 138.5–139 m. Procureur et al. 2023 say the pyramid is 139 m high today.
disagreements.why: 139 m is a rounded statement in the muon paper. 138.5 m is the figure used for the truncated core, at the bottom of that rounding.

disagreements.chosen: 5.229 m north–south and 5.752 m east–west (Petrie 205.85 by 226.47 inches)
disagreements.range: Many secondary accounts, including Wikipedia, swap the two axes.
disagreements.why: Petrie's wall-by-wall table measures 205.85 inches from north wall to south wall and 226.47 inches from west wall to east wall. He also notes that this north–south width matches the King's Chamber.

disagreements.chosen: Horizontal void, 30 m long, Grand Gallery cross-section, centred 20 m north of the pyramid centre with its floor set so the centre is 45 m from the Queen's Chamber
disagreements.range: Length is a minimum. The 2017 paper leaves the void horizontal or inclined, and possibly several adjacent spaces. No centreline coordinates were published.
disagreements.why: The horizontal hypothesis is one of the two drawn in Procureur et al. 2023, figure 1. The placement satisfies the constraints that were published: above the gallery, at least 30 m, similar cross-section, 40–50 m from the Queen's Chamber.
